reasons: Hypothesis fit: the original asks which of two accounts holds (continuation vs. give-back); the agent chose the give-back arm with an adaptive threshold, session-context filter, and one-bar pullback confirmation. That is squarely inside the family and the code executes a fade of the outsized bar in the direction opposite to it, matching the docstring's claim.

Train economics are internally consistent: net +1292.75 points (~$25.9k) on gross +1829.55 points with 2684 trades over 384 sessions (~7 trades/session) and ~35min average holds on 5m bars. Not a degenerate optimum; trade count and turnover (14.6 contracts/session at size=1) are plausible for NQ.

Commission is 536.8 / 1829.55 ≈ 29.3% of gross — heavy but does not flip the sign of P&L, so costs do not 'decide' the outcome on the train split. Fill at $2/contract/side (0.1 points) is realistic for retail futures.
Neither of the two listed artifact patterns (positive score with negative net P&L; inactivity-maximised score) is present in the train evidence.
